model_annotations.Bulgarian: This donut chart visually compares the proportions of different character types, categorized into two main groups: “Virtual Characters” and “Real Characters,” with the latter further subdivided. The outer ring, representing “Virtual Characters,” is divided into six light blue segments labeled “Comic Characters,” “Movie Characters,” “Teleplay Characters,” “Novel Characters,” “Game Characters,” and “Custom Characters.” The inner ring, representing “Real Characters,” is divided into seven green segments labeled “Scientists,” “Artists,” “Athletes,” “Writers,” “Musicians,” “Actors,” and “Influencers.” The chart includes a legend that clarifies the color coding for each category, and percentage values are displayed inside each slice. The “Virtual Characters” category occupies the largest portion of the chart, while “Real Characters” is smaller and further subdivided. The segments appear to be arranged in descending order of size within each ring, with “Comic Characters” being the largest in the outer ring and “Custom Characters” being the smallest. The “Custom Characters” slice is visually emphasized by being slightly exploded or offset from the center.

The outer ring is divided into eight distinct slices, each representing a different character type: “Comic Characters,” “Movie Characters,” “Teleplay Characters,” “Novel Characters,” “Game Characters,” “Custom Characters,” “Scientists,” “Artists,” “Athletes,” “Writers,” “Musicians,” “Actors,” and “Influencers.” The “Virtual Characters” category is depicted in a medium blue, while “Real Characters” is shown in green, and “Custom Characters” is highlighted in a distinct pink. The chart lacks percentage labels within the slices or a legend, and the segments are arranged in a clockwise order from the top, starting with “Comic Characters,” followed by “Movie Characters,” “Teleplay Characters,” “Novel Characters,” “Game Characters,” “Custom Characters,” and then the “Real Characters” group which contains the remaining seven subcategories. The “Virtual Characters” section occupies the largest area of the chart, suggesting it encompasses the majority of the data being represented.

The inner ring, colored green, is labeled “Real Characters” and is further subdivided into six smaller segments: “Scientists,” “Artists,” “Athletes,” “Writers,” “Musicians,” and “Actors/Influencers,” each with a distinct green shade. The chart lacks a legend or percentage labels inside the slices, and no slices are visually emphasized through explosion or bolding.
